title: Idempotent Pipelines
content:
Golden rule of data engineering: Pipelines must be idempotent.

Idempotent = running it twice produces the same result as running once.

Bad (not idempotent):
  INSERT INTO target SELECT * FROM source WHERE date = today
  -- Running twice = duplicate rows!

Good (idempotent):
  MERGE INTO target USING source
  ON target.id = source.id
  WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE
  WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT
  -- Running twice = same result

Also good:
  DELETE + INSERT (replace partition)
  CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE

If your pipeline can't safely re-run, it's broken.

#DataEngineering #BestPractices #Idempotency

title: MERGE Statement
content:
MERGE: The most important DML for data engineers.

MERGE INTO target t
USING source s
ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at > t.updated_at THEN
  UPDATE SET t.name = s.name, t.amount = s.amount
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
  INSERT (id, name, amount) VALUES (s.id, s.name, s.amount)
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN
  DELETE;

This single statement handles:
- Inserts (new records)
- Updates (changed records)
- Deletes (removed records)

title: Snowflake QUALIFY Clause
content:
QUALIFY: Snowflake's secret weapon for deduplication.

Without QUALIFY (verbose):
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn
  FROM events
) WHERE rn = 1;

With QUALIFY (clean):
SELECT *
FROM events
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1;

Same result. No subquery. More readable.

QUALIFY works like WHERE but filters AFTER window functions.

Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery support it. PostgreSQL doesn't.
